([[Middle Village, Queens|Middle Village, New York]]) | college = [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] (2017–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]] | team2 = →[[Birmingham Squadron]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team3 = [[New York Knicks]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ({{nbafy|2026}}) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Defensive Player of the Year (2021) * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2021) * Third-team All-ACC (2020) }} '''Jose Alvarado''' (born April 12, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) since 2026. He is nicknamed "'''Grand Theft Alvarado'''" for his exceptional ability to generate [[Steal (basketball)|steals]], as well as his defensive prowess.{{cite news |url=https://www.fox8live.com/2022/11/12/undrafted-rookie-household-name-grand-theft-alvarados-cult-following-grows-with-pels-hype/ |last=Roberson |first=Josh |title=From undrafted rookie to household name, 'Grand Theft Alvarado's cult following grows with Pels hype | work=FOX 8 |date=November 12, 2022}} Before joining the NBA, he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] from 2017 to 2021. Since 2022, he has also represented [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|Puerto Rico]] in international competitions, including the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]]. When the Knicks beat the Spurs in the [[2026 NBA Finals]], he became the third Puerto Rican to win a championship, after [[Butch Lee]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in [[1980 NBA Finals|1980]], and [[J. J. Barea]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in [[2011 NBA Finals|2011]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/jose-alvarado-nuevo-campeon-boricua-en-la-nba-lleva-la-bandera-de-puerto-rico-al-festejo/ |last=Figueroa Loza |first=Jorge |title=José Alvarado, nuevo campeón boricua en la NBA, lleva la bandera de Puerto Rico al festejo | trans-title=José Alvarado, the new Puerto Rican NBA champion, carries the Puerto Rican flag to the celebration | work=[[El Nuevo Día]] |date=June 14, 2026 |language=es}} He is currently the only native New Yorker on the Knicks' roster.{{Cite news | url=https://www.npr.org/2026/06/13/nx-s1-5854641/jose-alvarado-is-the-only-native-new-yorker-on-the-knicks-roster-fans-react | title=Jose Alvarado is the only native New Yorker on the Knicks' roster. Fans react | first=Samantha | last=Max | work=[[NPR]] | date=June 13, 2026}} == Early life == Alvarado was born in [[Brooklyn]]. His father, Jose Alvarado Sr., is an electrician of Puerto Rican descent and his mother, Odilia Martinez, is of Mexican descent and was a stay-at-home mom.{{Cite news | url=https://nypost.com/2026/06/09/sports/jose-alvarados-former-coaches-reveal-how-he-got-to-the-knicks/ | title=How the Knicks’ Jose Alvarado ‘fought’ his way home to NYC — and why ‘everything about him screams New York’: former coach | first=Jeanette | last=Settembre | work=[[New York Post]] | date=June 9, 2026}} He lived in [[Lindsay Park (housing cooperative)|Lindsay Park]] in [[Williamsburg, Brooklyn]] and the Pomonok Houses [[public housing]] project in [[Pomonok, Queens]]. Alvarado played [[American football|football]] in his childhood but quit after injuring his neck.{{cite news |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/the-spirit-tech-basketball-jose-alvarado-attacks-one-complex-life/54l7lnyG0WTECshJpGb0NJ/ |last=Hummer |first=Steve |title=The spirit of Tech basketball, Jose Alvarado attacks one complex life |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=March 5, 2020}} He attended PS 200 in Queens for elementary school and played [[Catholic Youth Organization]] basketball at St Ann's in Flushing, Queens. He has stated that this experience, provided by his parents, is where his passion for the game developed.{{Cite news | url=https://thetablet.org/former-cyo-and-ck-hoops-standout-now-plays-in-nba/ | title=Former CYO and CK Hoops Standout Now Plays in NBA | first=Jim | last=Mancari | work=The Tablet | date=January 27, 2022}} He later played basketball for [[Christ the King Regional High School]] in [[Middle Village, Queens]], in New York City. As a junior, Alvarado averaged 17 points and 6.5 assists per game and was named [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) Player of the Year.{{cite news |url=https://www.qchron.com/editions/central/christ-the-king-s-jose-alvarado-wins-mvp/article_2a10a482-37df-5bf1-a33e-1ba389aadea4.html |last1=Barca |first1=Christopher |title=Christ the King's Jose Alvarado wins MVP |work=[[Queens Chronicle]] |date=February 25, 2016}} As a senior, he recorded 18 points, 10 rebounds, 10 assists and 10 steals, the first [[Double-double#Quadruple-double|quadruple-double]] in school history, in a December 22, 2016, win over [[Xaverian High School]].{{cite news |url=https://dailyorange.com/2020/02/georgia-tech-jose-alvarado-all-around-game-irreplaceable/ |last=McKeon |first=Cameron |title=Georgia Tech's Jose Alvarado's all-around game makes him irreplaceable |work=[[The Daily Orange]] |date=February 22, 2020}} In his senior season, Alvarado averaged 17.9 points per game and led Christ the King to the CHSAA intersectional quarterfinals. He was named [[TimesLedger Newspapers|TimesLedger]] Player of the Year.{{cite news |url=https://qns.com/story/2017/04/24/royal-reign-alvarado-tops-in-queens/ |last=Amato |first=Laura |title=Royal reign: Alvarado tops in Queens | work=[[Schneps Media]] |date=April 24, 2017}} Alvarado was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and a three-star recruit by [[247Sports.com]] in the 2017 class.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/216121/jose-alvarado |title=Jose Alvarado – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles | work=[[ESPN]]}}{{Cite web |url=https://247sports.com/player/jose-alvarado-85143/ |title=Jose Alvarado, 2017 Point guard |publisher=[[247Sports.com]]}} In September 2016, he committed to play college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] over offers from [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], among others.{{cite news |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/pastner-lands-point-guard-jose-alvarado-first-commit-2017-class/kYSAByedK9J339FHyETtMK/ |last=Sugiura |first=Ken |title=Pastner lands point guard Jose Alvarado, first commit of 2017 class |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=September 15, 2016}} Georgia Tech head coach [[Josh Pastner]] had first seen Alvarado at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]].{{cite news |url=https://www.macon.com/sports/college/acc/georgia-tech/article196756999.html |last=Awtrey |first=Stan |title=Tech's freshman, Alvarado started in all 25 of his games and averaged 12.1 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. He became the fourth Georgia Tech freshman to average at least 12 points, 3.5 rebounds, and two assists per game.{{cite news |url=https://yellowjackedup.com/2018/03/23/georgia-tech-basketball-alvarados-quiet-but-special-freshman-season/ |last=Callaghan-Croley |first=Dylan |title=Alvarado's quiet but special freshman season |work=[[FanSided]] |date=March 23, 2018}} He suffered a season-ending left elbow fracture against [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] on February 11, 2018.{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/02/12/georgia-techs-jose-alvarado-to-miss-remainder-of-season/110340476/ |title=Georgia Tech's Jose Alvarado to miss remainder of season |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 12, 2018}} Alvarado had an increased role in his sophomore season with the early departure of [[Josh Okogie]].{{cite news |url=https://accsports.com/acc-analytics/better-know-player-gt-jose-alvarado/ |last=Geisinger |first=Brian |title=Better Know a Player: Now healthy, Is Georgia Tech's Jose Alvarado ready for a bigger role? | work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=July 11, 2018}} On February 20, 2019, Alvarado scored a career-high 29 points to go with 6 rebounds and 5 assists in a 73–65 win over [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].{{cite news | url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/college/acc/georgia_tech/jose-alvarado-s-career-high-leads-georgia-tech-over-pitt/article_1f652414-5c42-5da3-9c9a-bafd77175dc5.html |title=Jose Alvarado's career-high 29 leads Georgia Tech over Pitt |work=[[Gwinnett Daily Post]] |date=February 20, 2019}} As a sophomore, Alvarado averaged 12.5 points, 3.9 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, leading his team in scoring, assists and steals.{{cite web |url=https://ramblinwreck.com/roster/jose-alvarado/ |title=#10 Jose Alvarado, G | work=[[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] |date=June 18, 2018}} Georgia Tech was banned from the postseason by the NCAA during his junior season due to several infractions. He missed seven games early in his junior season due to an ankle injury.{{cite news |url=https://www.macon.com/sports/college/acc/georgia-tech/article239326873.html |last=Awtrey |first=Stan |title=Since the return of this point guard, Georgia Tech has looked like a different basketball team |work=[[The Telegraph (Macon)|The Telegraph]] |date=January 15, 2020}} On January 25, 2020, Alvarado scored a season-high 26 points and recorded 8 rebounds and a school-record nine steals in a 64–58 victory over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].{{cite news |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/after-review-georgia-tech-jose-alvarado-awarded-school-steal-record/sB8cLEKa6VcJ1Nf0i3JP5N/ |last=Sugiura |first=Ken |title=After review, Georgia Tech's Jose Alvarado awarded school steal record |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=January 26, 2020}} In his junior season, he averaged 14.4 points, four assists, 3.4 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game and was named to the Third Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). In his senior year, Alvarado and [[Moses Wright]] led Georgia Tech to its first ACC title since 1993, by defeating [[Scottie Barnes]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] in the championship game of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/mark-bradley-blog/a-return-to-glory-georgia-tech-wins-the-acc-title/7N356OMRSVAD3O5IZU3IE3O7FE/ |title=A return to glory: Georgia Tech wins the ACC title |last=Bradley |first=Mark |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=March 14, 2021}} At the end of the season, he was named the ACC Defensive Player of the Year.{{Cite news |url=https://www.wtkr.com/sports/acc-announces-2020-21-mens-basketball-awards-hokies-young-named-coach-of-the-year |title=ACC announces 2020-21 men's basketball awards; Hokies' Young named Coach of the Year | work=[[WTKR]] |date=March 8, 2021}}{{Cite news |url=https://theacc.com/news/2021/3/7/acc-announces-mens-basketball-awards.aspx |title=ACC Men's Basketball Awards Announced |work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 8, 2021}} Alvarado graduated from Georgia Tech in 2021 with a degree in literature, media and communications.{{cite web |url=https://ramblinwreck.com/roster/jose-alvarado/ |title=#10 Jose Alvarado |work=ramblinwreck.com |publisher=Georgia Tech Athletics}} ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Pelicans / Birmingham Squadron (2021–2026)=== Alvarado passed on gaining an additional year in college due to [[COVID-19]] game cancellations and declared himself eligible for the [[2021 NBA draft]]. After being undrafted, on August 19, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Under the terms of the deal, he split time with the Pelicans and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite news |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-jose-alvarado-and-daulton-hommes-two-way-contracts |title=Pelicans sign Jose Alvarado and Daulton Hommes to two-way contracts |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |date=August 19, 2021}} During a game against the [[2021–22 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]] on January 25, 2022, Alvarado was issued a [[technical foul]] after an in-game verbal altercation with Philadelphia center [[Joel Embiid]]. Embiid praised Alvarado and paid the associated $2,000 league fine.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33163524/philadelphia-76ers-joel-embiid-pays-new-orleans-pelicans-rookie-jose-alvarado-fine-spat |first=Andrew |last=Lopez |title=Philadelphia 76ers' Joel Embiid pays New Orleans Pelicans rookie Jose Alvarado's fine after spat | work=[[ESPN]] |date=January 27, 2022}} On March 28, Alvarado's two-way deal was converted into a standard four-year, $6.5 million contract.{{cite news | url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-jose-alvarado-multi-year-contract|title=Pelicans sign Jose Alvarado to multi-year contract |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] | date=March 28, 2022}}{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33616869/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-point-guard-jose-alvarado-multi-year-contract | title=Pelicans sign PG Alvarado to multiyear contract |first=Andrew |last=Lopez | work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 28, 2022}} This signing made him eligible for post-season play. In 2022, Alvarado gained social media traction for highlight clips of him creating steals by sneaking up behind the opposing team's ball handler, which also led to his nickname "Grand Theft Alvarado".{{Cite magazine | url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/basketball/jose-alvarado-pelicans-player-season-preview |last=Kimble | first=Terry |title=Jose Alvarado, The People's Champ: Pelicans Player Season Preview | magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=September 15, 2022}}{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pelicans-jose-alvarado-is-still-sneaking-up-on-the-nba-he-just-plays-fierce/ |title=Pelicans' Jose Alvarado is still sneaking up on the NBA: 'He just plays fierce' |work=[[CBS Sports]] |orig-date=November 14, 2022 |date=February 17, 2023}} On December 4, 2022, Alvarado scored a career-high 38 points in a 121–106 win over the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{cite news |title=Jose Alvarado sets insane mark not seen since 1970 |url=https://clutchpoints.com/pelicans-news-jose-alvarado-sets-insane-mark-not-seen-since-1970 |work=ClutchPoints |last=Sabri |first=Alex |date=December 4, 2022}} On February 17, 2023, he won the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] MVP award after hitting the game-winning shot.{{Cite web |title=Pelicans' Jose Alvarado steals show, wins Rising Stars MVP |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35684123/pelicans-jose-alvarado-steals-show-wins-rising-stars-mvp |access-date=February 22, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 18, 2023}} On February 28, Alvarado suffered a stress reaction in his right tibia.{{cite news | last=Clark | first=Christian | title=Pelicans say Jose Alvarado and Larry Nance Jr. will miss multiple weeks | work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]] | date=February 28, 2023 | url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/alvarado-and-nance-to-miss-multiple-weeks/article_9ace96d0-b7c9-11ed-bb7e-3bd9c1a4c209.html | access-date=2025-12-02}} On March 22, the Pelicans announced that Alvarado would be sidelined for at least another two-to-three weeks, ending his season.{{Cite news |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-medical-updates-zion-williamson-jose-alvarado-032223 |title=New Orleans Pelicans announce medical updates |work=[[National Basketball Association]] | date=March 22, 2023}} Alvarado made 56 appearances off of the bench for New Orleans during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], posting averages of 7.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.1 steals.{{Cite web|title=Jose Alvarado 2023–24 Stats per Game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277869/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=March 6, 2026 | work=[[ESPN]]}} On September 28, 2024, Alvarado signed a two-year, $9 million contract extension with New Orleans.{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41496848/pelicans-extend-jose-alvarado-2-year-9m-deal | title=Sources: Pels extend Alvarado for 2 years, $9M | work=[[ESPN]] |date=September 28, 2024}} He played in 56 games (including 23 starts) for the Pelicans during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], averaging career-highs in points (10.3), rebounds (2.4), assists (4.6), and steals (1.3).{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277869/type/nba/year/2025 |title=Jose Alvarado 2024–25 Stats per Game |work=[[ESPN]]}} Alvarado played in 41 games for the Pelicans during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 7.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 3.1 assists.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277869/type/nba/year/2026 |title=Jose Alvarado 2025–26 Stats per Game |work=[[ESPN]]}} ===New York Knicks (2026–present)=== On February 5, 2026, Alvarado was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Dalen Terry]] and two future second round draft picks.{{Cite news |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-jose-alvarado |title=NEW YORK KNICKS ACQUIRE JOSE ALVARADO |work=[[National Basketball Association]] | date=February 5, 2026}}{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47839301/sources-knicks-acquiring-pg-jose-alvarado-pelicans |title=Sources: Knicks acquiring PG Jose Alvarado from Pelicans |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 5, 2026}} As a native New Yorker returning home, Alvarado immediately endeared himself to Knicks fans through his energy, hustle, and active defense.{{cite news |url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/knicks-analysis/79800/jose-alvarado-has-been-everything-the-knicks-were-looking-for-and-more |first=Sam |last=Stein |title=Jose Alvarado has been everything the Knicks were looking for (and more) | work=[[SB Nation]] |date=March 3, 2026}} Within a week, at a February 11 away game against the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]], Alvarado became the first player in Knicks franchise history to record 25+ points, 5+ steals, and 5+ three-pointers in a game off the bench. Alvarado scored 26 points and made 8 of his 13 three-point attempts, leading to a 138-89 victory for the Knicks over the 76ers. After playing sparingly in the [[2026 NBA Finals]], Alvarado suited up for Game 4 of the Finals. In the game, Alvarado played a key role off the bench. He played most of the 4th quarter and hit multiple three-point shots, including scoring five straight Knick points to keep the Spurs from pulling away, thus, helping the Knicks come back from down 29 points, the largest comeback win in NBA Finals history. In the game, Alvarado tallied 8 points, 3 rebounds, and 2 assists in 16 minutes of play time.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/news/jose-alvarado-game-4-feature | last=Zillgitt | first=Jeff | title=Jose Alvarado provides unlikely boost in crunch time for the Knicks | work=[[National Basketball Association]] | date=June 10, 2026}} In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Alvarado helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs |title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs |work=ClutchPoints |last=Siegel |first=Brett |date=June 13, 2026 |access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973 |title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship |work=NBA.com |last=Lambert |first=Ben |date=June 13, 2026 |access-date=June 13, 2026}} On June 26, 2026, Alvarado declined his $4.5 million player option and re-signed with the Knicks on a three-year, $14 million contract.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Jose Alvarado returning to Knicks on new 3-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49190706/jose-alvarado-returning-new-york-knicks-new-3-year-deal|access-date=June 30, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en|date=June 26, 2026|last=Charania|first=Shams}}{{cite web|title=NEW YORK KNICKS RE-SIGN JOSE ALVARADO|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-re-sign-jose-alvarado|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2026|access-date=July 13, 2026}} ==National team career== Although a native of [[Brooklyn]], Alvarado represents [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|Puerto Rico]] at the international level due to his Puerto Rican ancestry.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/.amp/basketball/jose-alvarado-playing-puerto-rico-national-basketball-team |title= Jose Alvarado to Play for Puerto Rico's National Basketball Team | first=Terry | last=Kimble |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 15, 2022|access-date=April 17, 2022}} Alvarado was recruited in 2022 by [[Carlos Arroyo]], retired team captain and current general manager.{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2022 |title=José Alvarado se prueba como boricua al declarar que quiere derrotar al Team USA|url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/jose-alvarado-se-prueba-como-boricua-al-declarar-que-quiere-derrotar-al-team-usa/|access-date=2024-07-07 |work=Primera Hora |language=es}} He was part of the team that helped Puerto Rico qualify for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]] after defeating both [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexico]] in the semifinals and [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]] in the final of one of four [[2024 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments]].{{cite web |title=Puerto Rico ends 20-year Olympic drought with historic win over Lithuania|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-olympic-qualifying-tournament-2024-san-juan-puerto-rico/news/puerto-rico-ends-20-year-olympic-draught-with-historic-win-over-lithuania |work=fiba.basketball |date=7 July 2024}} He was named [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the [[2024 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments – San Juan|tournament]] after he averaged 16.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.3 steals, and had a 29-point performance against Italy and 23 points against Lithuania.{{cite web |title=Alvarado earns TISSOT MVP honors at the FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament in San Juan|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-olympic-qualifying-tournament-2024-san-juan-puerto-rico/news/alvarado-earns-tissot-mvp-honors-at-the-fiba-olympic-qualifying-tournament
